Inventory summaries with aggregates

Unit 2 · Week 5 · Lesson 3 · Suggested 55-minute plan; adjust to local timing.

Prepare: Open a fresh working copy of database-project.sqlite in a school-approved SQLite tool. Keep sql-starter.sqlite unchanged. The project edition adds Equipment.ReplacementCost. Review database-project-setup.sql and use database-project-workbook.md, database-project-answers.md and database-project-reports.sql. Use fictional data and public explained answers. No cloud account is required. These 55-minute timings are flexible.

Suggested answers are teacher guidance, not extra assessment tasks. These notes are public.

1. Inventory summaries with aggregates

Suggested time: 2 minutes

Instructional strategy: Learning intention

Use the separate database-project.sqlite edition of the equipment desk. ReplacementCost contains fictional whole-dollar teaching estimates, not current prices. Activities are ungraded. This week practises joins and summaries; controlled changes follow in Week 6. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#database-solution.

2. What one input row represents

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Recall and prediction

Equipment has one row per physical item. Loan has one row per event, so E02 occurs twice in its history. Starting with joined history can duplicate the cost for E02 or omit unused items. Choose input rows to match the question. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#database-solution.

3. Fictional replacement estimates

Suggested time: 6 minutes

Instructional strategy: Worked example

These are fixed fictional teaching values, not market prices. Five items total 1400. Mean 280, minimum 80 and maximum 600. Ask learners to calculate by hand before SQL. ReplacementCost is added in database-project.sqlite, not the previous SQL-basics starter. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#database-solution.

4. An inventory summary

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Teacher model with predictions

The complete single-row result is 5, 1400, 280.0, 80, 600. Each aggregate summarises the Equipment input rows. AS gives readable result headings. Numeric summaries should use meaningful numeric attributes, not arbitrary identifiers. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#database-solution.

5. The five summary values

Suggested time: 10 minutes

Instructional strategy: Guided paired practice

Costs are whole-dollar estimates; the sum, mean, minimum and maximum carry dollar units. COUNT(*) is a row count. COUNT(field) counts non-NULL values of that field. SUM, AVG, MIN and MAX ignore NULL input values. Do not confuse a row count with a distinct item count after a join. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#database-solution.

6. A summary with evidence

Suggested time: 12 minutes

Instructional strategy: Independent application

Joined loan history has six rows and counts E02 cost 80 twice in the supplied data, yielding 1480 rather than inventory total 1400. For ungrouped aggregates over empty C99 input, expect one row: COUNT(*) 0, other four aggregates NULL. NULL is not automatically zero. A GROUP BY query with no input groups returns no rows. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#database-solution.

7. Zero rows and a NULL sum

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Misconception check with reasons

COUNT counts zero input rows. SQLite SUM returns NULL when there are no non-NULL inputs. An ungrouped aggregate query still returns one summary row. Do not label NULL as a measured zero cost. The distinction affects how a report communicates missing or absent values. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#database-solution.

8. A repeated cost is not a repeated item

Suggested time: 5 minutes

Instructional strategy: Reflection and a fresh example

No. It removes repeated numeric values, which might belong to different real items. Correct the input rows and relationships instead. Compute inventory from Equipment, where each physical item is represented once. A repair must preserve two distinct items even if they have equal costs. Teaching source: https://edugenio.github.io/cs-atar-textbook/#database-solution.
